newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka economic growth seen at 6.5 pct - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka economic growth seen at 6.5 pct - paper.

text.p: Sri Lanka should achieve an economic growth rate of 6.5 percent over the next few years if present government policies are maintained, the government-run Daily News said on Thursday.
The newspaper quoted the chairman of the Industrial Association of Sri Lanka, Cubby Wijetunge, as saying the economic situation was definitely sounder than in the previous two years.
Sri Lankan gross domestic product grew by 3.8 percent in 1996, down from 5.5 percent the year before, mainly because of a drought which caused widespread power cuts to industry.
Wijetunge said he expected industrial output to grow 10 percent this year, up from 7.5 percent in 1996 and 10.2 percent in 1995.

He said major hurdles in achieving higher growth were the country's high budget deficit and the massive cost of the war, which is being fought by government forces and rebels of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).
The LTTE want a separate homeland for the minority Tamil population in the Indian Ocean island's east and north.
Wijetunge said Sri Lankan unemployment stood at around 11 to 13 percent.
